observations.text: SP flew the fingertip position with the IP directing the geometry and applying part of the control and power inputs, which corresponds to the level required for this stage. Lateral separation drifted to 26 ft against the 10 ft reference and the observance angle opened beyond 55 degrees before each IP directed correction. Marginal performance for the Training Section; earlier recognition of the closure trend and a reduced dependence on IP directed inputs are expected to improve.

SP, as wingman, preserved the fingertip position and completed the climbs, descents and turns after the IP's verbal advisories on closure and stack, without any intervention on the controls. Lateral separation peaked at 20 ft beyond the 10 ft reference and the A/C was flown 10 ft low on the stack, at the code 1 limits, with the deviations recognized and corrected with delay. Overtake was contained with the speed brake on the leader's command. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP controlled the A/C in a smooth and solid way, without abrupt corrections, and preserved the fingertip position through the turns and the modified Lazy Eights, using the engine power properly and trimming continuously. Lateral separation opened to 15 ft beyond the 10 ft reference and the observance angle reached about 40 degrees, between the code 3 and the code 1 values, with both deviations self-detected and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP preserved the position determined in the Techniques and Procedures Manual on both sides of the leading A/C, holding the observance angle within 30 degrees plus or minus 5 degrees and the stack within 3 ft of the briefed reference. Lateral separation remained within 8 ft of the 10 ft reference and the speed brake was used correctly to keep overtake under control. All corrections were accurate and prompt and no IP prompting was required. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the fingertip position with exceptional precision on both sides of the leading A/C, with lateral separation held within 2 ft of the 10 ft reference and the stack within 1 ft of the briefed value. The observance angle was kept within 1 degree of 30 degrees through the climbs, descents, turns and modified Lazy Eights, with continuous trimming and anticipatory use of the engine power. Deviations were negligible and no prompting was required at any point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to late and coarse power corrections on an out of trim A/C, did not control the A/C in a smooth and solid way and did not preserve the fingertip position during the turns, with the result of lateral separation reaching 30 ft against the 10 ft reference and the stack 16 ft low, beyond the code 1 limits. The IP directed the corrections and applied part of the control and power inputs to re-establish the position. Further practice in power management and trim technique in close formation is required.

SP, due to a perceptual error in judging closure and lateral separation, did not use the speed brake to keep overtake under control and did not preserve the position determined in the Techniques and Procedures Manual, with the result of an observance angle opening beyond 60 degrees and lateral separation closing inside the 10 ft reference. The IP took the A/C to open the geometry and directed the subsequent rejoin to fingertip. Further training in closure assessment and speed brake usage from both sides is required.

SP preserved the fingertip position and completed the climbs, descents and turns at the level required for this stage, with the corrections applied after the IP's verbal advisories and without any intervention on the controls. Lateral separation reached 19 ft beyond the 10 ft reference and the stack 9 ft low, just inside the code 1 limits, and the deviations were recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section; earlier detection of the closure trend and a reduced dependence on IP prompting are expected to improve.

SP controlled the A/C smoothly and solidly, without abrupt corrections, and used the engine power and trim continuously to preserve the fingertip position through the modified Lazy Eights. Lateral separation opened to 17 ft against the 10 ft reference and the stack varied 6 ft low, between the code 3 and the code 1 values, with both deviations self-detected and corrected in a timely manner and without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, as leader, executed and completed the planned climbs, descents, turns and modified Lazy Eights smoothly, maintaining positive pressure on the flying controls so that No2 could stay in position. Bank was increased to 90 degrees on the Lazy Eight type maneuvers with airspeed contained between 85 and 100 KIAS and never below the 120 KIAS minimum in the level phases, and the wingman's position with regard to the sun and the flight area borders was taken into account before each reversal. Execution was accurate, prompt and proficient throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew as wingman with exceptional precision, holding lateral separation within 2 ft of the 10 ft reference and the stack within 1 ft through the climbs, descents, turns and modified Lazy Eights. The observance angle was maintained at 30 degrees with deviations not exceeding 2 degrees, the A/C was continuously trimmed and the speed brake was used from both sides on the leader's command, keeping overtake under control at all times. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to abrupt pitch corrections and a delayed power reduction in the descending turn, did not control the A/C in a smooth and solid way and did not preserve the vertical position of the fingertip formation, with the result of the A/C being flown 18 ft below the briefed stack, beyond the 10 ft code 1 limit. The IP intervened on the controls to arrest the sink and directed the recovery to the fingertip position. Further practice in smooth pitch and power control in close formation is required.

SP, due to a physical environment factor, glare on the canopy during the turn into the sun, did not preserve the position determined in the Techniques and Procedures Manual and did not use the speed brake to keep overtake under control, with the result of lateral separation closing inside the 10 ft reference and an observance angle exceeding 60 degrees. The IP took the A/C, opened the separation and directed the re-establishment of the fingertip position. Further practice in reference retention with adverse sun position is required.

SP, due to a non-standard sight picture on the leading A/C wing tip and fuselage line, did not preserve the position determined in the Techniques and Procedures Manual during the turns, with the result of an observance angle stabilized at 50 degrees and lateral separation 20 ft beyond the 10 ft reference, at the code 1 limits. The deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, only after the IP's verbal prompts, with no intervention on the controls.

SP, due to an interrupted cross-check of the leader's reference line while attention remained inside the cockpit, did not maintain the fingertip stack and did not trim the A/C continuously, with the result of the A/C settling 10 ft below the briefed stack, at the code 1 limit. The stack error was recognized and corrected with delay after the IP's verbal prompt, without intervention on the controls. An increased frequency of the outside reference scan is required.

SP preserved the fingertip position on both sides of the leading A/C within the desired standards, using the engine power properly and trimming the A/C without abrupt corrections. Lateral separation twice opened to 16 ft against the 10 ft reference and the stack varied 6 ft low during the modified Lazy Eights, with the deviations self-detected and corrected in a timely manner and without the IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section; a tighter control of the observance angle through the high bank phases is expected to improve.

SP controlled the A/C in a smooth and solid way, without abrupt corrections, applying anticipatory power and continuous trim in both fingertip positions. Lateral separation was held within 7 ft of the 10 ft reference, the stack within 3 ft and the observance angle within 30 degrees plus or minus 5 degrees through the climbs, descents and turns, with the speed brake used correctly from both sides to keep overtake under control. All corrections were accurate and prompt and no IP prompting was required. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, as leader, executed and completed the planned maneuvers smoothly and maintained positive pressure on the flying controls throughout the modified Lazy Eights, which allowed No2 to stay in the fingertip position without large corrections. Bank was progressively increased to 90 degrees with airspeed contained between 85 and 100 KIAS and the load kept between 2 and 3 Gs, and the wingman's position with regard to the sun and the flight area borders was accounted for before each reversal. Deviations from the planned profile were negligible. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to over-controlled inputs in roll and a late power reduction on the rejoin to fingertip, did not control the A/C in a smooth and solid way and did not preserve the position determined in the Techniques and Procedures Manual, with the result of lateral separation reaching 32 ft against the 10 ft reference and the stack 14 ft low, beyond the code 1 limits. The IP directed the corrections and applied part of the control inputs to re-establish the fingertip position. Further practice in close formation control inputs and power anticipation is required.

SP, due to failure to make the knock-it-off call when the briefed formation parameters were exceeded, did not use the speed brake to keep overtake under control and did not preserve the fingertip position during the descending turn, with the result of an observance angle exceeding 65 degrees and lateral separation reducing inside the 10 ft reference. The IP took the A/C to open the geometry and terminated the maneuver. Knock-it-off discipline and speed brake technique from both sides require further training.

SP, due to a fixation on the leading A/C nose instead of the briefed wing tip and canopy references, did not preserve the position determined in the Techniques and Procedures Manual through the turns, with the result of an observance angle held at 50 degrees and the stack 6 ft high, at the code 1 limits. The corrections were applied with delay and only after the IP's verbal advisories, with no intervention on the controls.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the modified Lazy Eights, did not use the engine power properly and did not trim the A/C continuously, with the result of lateral separation reaching 20 ft beyond the 10 ft reference, at the code 1 limit, and repeated overtake that was contained only after the IP's verbal advisory to extend the speed brake. The deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, without intervention on the controls. Further practice in power anticipation and speed brake usage from both sides is required.

SP, due to slightly late power corrections at the transition from the climb to level flight, did not hold the fingertip stack constant, with the result of the A/C varying 6 ft below the briefed stack, between the code 3 and the code 1 values. The deviation was self-detected and corrected in a timely manner, without abrupt inputs and without the IP's intervention.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established in the fingertip position, did not preserve the lateral separation determined in the Techniques and Procedures Manual during the turn away, with the result of lateral separation opening to 16 ft beyond the 10 ft reference and an observance angle of about 40 degrees. The A/C was returned to position with smooth control and power inputs, the deviation being recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP preserved the fingertip position on both sides of the leading A/C within the desired standards, trimming continuously, using the engine power properly and extending the speed brake on the leader's command to keep overtake under control. Lateral separation remained within 9 ft of the 10 ft reference and the stack within 4 ft, at the edge of the code 3 band during the modified Lazy Eights. Marginal performance for the Training Section; a steadier observance angle through the high bank phases is expected to improve with practice.

SP flew both fingertip positions with exceptional precision, holding lateral separation within 2 ft of the 10 ft reference, the stack within 1 ft and the observance angle within 2 degrees of 30 degrees through the climbs, descents, turns and modified Lazy Eights. The A/C was controlled smoothly and solidly, with no abrupt corrections, anticipatory power and continuous trim, and the speed brake was used from both sides without prompting to keep overtake under control. Deviations were negligible at all times. Above end of block MIF achieved.
